AVGO reports paying $5,216 million in these taxes for fiscal 2024 (withholding ~38 million shares), whereas AMD reports a smaller outflow of $728 million for the same purpose in fiscal 2024.

comparisons.peer_topic: Fiscal 2024 Share Repurchase Activity and Authorization
comparisons.peer_summary: In fiscal year 2024, the company repurchased 21 million shares for $9.7 billion, bringing the total remaining authorization to $22.5 billion as of January 28, 2024. The program aims to offset dilution and includes post-year-end repurchases under a Rule 10b5-1 plan, with plans to continue repurchases in the current fiscal year.
comparisons.comparison: While AVGO discloses specific tax withholding amounts on net-settled equity awards, NVDA discloses the operational purpose of its share repurchase program, explicitly stating it aims to offset dilution from shares issued to employees. AVGO’s disclosure of net-settled awards represents a direct mechanical method of handling employee equity compensation taxes, whereas NVDA highlights the broader strategic goal of offsetting such dilution through open market repurchases.
